51481839.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human N-terminal TEV cleavable 6His tagged p47phox (151-285 residues) assessed as dissociation rate constant by Surface plasmon resonance assay

original_paragraph.Supporting Information S1: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments were performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare) at 25 °C. The human N-terminal TEV cleavable 6His tagged p47phox (151-285 residues) was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip (GE Healthcare) via amine coupling. The immobilization was performed at pH 4.0 using 10 mM sodium acetate buffer. The ligand was captured at a flow rate of 5 μL/min and a concentration of 10 μg/mL. The immobilized p47phox was then treated with 10 mM TEV protease in 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, 0.05% Tween-20 for 1 h at room temperature to remove the N-terminal tag. The sensor surface was regenerated with 10 mM glycine-HCl, pH 2.0, for 30 s. The analytes were injected at concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 100 μM in HBS-EP buffer (10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.005% P20) at a flow rate of 30 μL/min. The association phase lasted 120 s, followed by a 120 s dissociation phase. The data were analyzed using Biacore T200 evaluation software. The dissociation rate constant (koff) was determined from the dissociation phase of the sensorgrams. The SPR ligand efficiency (LE) was calculated as LE = -log(Kd) / molecular weight (in kDa).
